mean: to be on one's mind, to find oneself curious about
lit: to come onto the mind: something lands in your thoughts and stays there

use.how: Xが気になる: X draws your attention by itself and won't let go (a worry, a curiosity, a person you like). It happens to you; you don't do it.

near.diff: 気にする is actively minding or worrying about something (を気にする); 気になる is something catching your attention on its own (が気になる).

cue: You keep glancing at your phone because the exam results come out today and you can't stop thinking about them.

ctx.s: 明日[あした]の天気[てんき]が{気[き]になる}。
ctx.en: I keep wondering about tomorrow's weather.

ctx.s: テストの結果[けっか]が{気[き]になって}、夜[よる]よく眠[ねむ]れなかった。
ctx.en: The test results were on my mind, so I couldn't sleep well.

ctx.s: 「あの映画[えいが]、ずっと{気[き]になってた}んだ。一緒[いっしょ]に行[い]かない？」
ctx.en: "I've been curious about that film for ages. Want to go together?"

ctx.s: 「何[なに]か{気[き]になる}ことがあったら、遠慮[えんりょ]なく聞[き]いてください。」
ctx.en: "If anything bothers you or you're unsure about something, please don't hesitate to ask."

ctx.s: 最近[さいきん]、同[おな]じクラスに{気[き]になる}人[ひと]がいる。
ctx.en: Lately there's someone in my class I can't stop thinking about.

ctx.s: 一度[いちど]{気[き]になりだす}と、壁[かべ]の小[ちい]さな傷[きず]まで目[め]につく。
ctx.en: Once it starts to bother you, you notice even the tiny scratches on the wall.

bad.s: 人[ひと]の目[め]を{気[き]になる}のはやめよう。
bad.en: (meant: let's stop worrying about what people think)
bad.why: Ki ni naru takes ga, not o. For actively minding what others think, the verb is ki ni suru: hito no me o ki ni suru.

bad.s: 「大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]、{気[き]にならないで}ください。」
bad.en: (meant: it's fine, please don't worry about it)
bad.why: You cannot ask someone not to have a thing catch their mind. The fixed reassurance is ki ni shinaide kudasai.

mean: to be careful, to watch out
lit: to attach one's mind (to something): keep your attention fixed on it

use.how: Xに気をつける: watch out for X; ～ように気をつける: take care to do ～. 気をつけて is the everyday 'take care' said when someone leaves.

near.diff: 気にする is worrying about something; 気をつける is taking care so that something bad does not happen.

cue: Your friend is heading out into an icy night and you want to tell them to watch their step.

ctx.s: 道[みち]が凍[こお]っているから、{気[き]をつけて}ね。
ctx.en: The roads are icy, so be careful.

ctx.s: 熱[あつ]いので、やけどに{気[き]をつけて}ください。
ctx.en: It's hot, so be careful not to burn yourself.

ctx.s: 「寒[さむ]くなりますので、お体[からだ]に{気[き]をつけて}ください。」
ctx.en: "It's getting cold, so please take care of yourself."

ctx.s: 最近[さいきん]は食[た]べ過[す]ぎないように{気[き]をつけて}いる。
ctx.en: These days I make a point of not overeating.

ctx.s: 「申[もう]し訳[わけ]ありません。次[つぎ]から{気[き]をつけます}。」
ctx.en: "I'm very sorry. I'll be more careful from now on."

ctx.s: 「足元[あしもと]に{気[き]をつけて}お降[お]りください。」
ctx.en: "Please mind your step as you get off."

bad.s: 駅[えき]に着[つ]いてから、財布[さいふ]がないことに{気[き]をつけた}。
bad.en: (meant: when I got to the station, I noticed my wallet was gone)
bad.why: Ki o tsukeru is taking care beforehand, not noticing. Noticing something is ki ga tsuku: saifu ga nai koto ni ki ga tsuita.

bad.s: 明日[あした]の試験[しけん]を{気[き]をつけて}いる。
bad.en: (meant: I'm worried about tomorrow's exam)
bad.why: Ki o tsukeru already has its o and means being careful, not worrying. Say shiken ga ki ni naru, or shiken o ki ni shite iru.

mean: to feel angry or offended at something
lit: the belly stands up: anger rising in the gut, the old seat of feelings

use.how: Xに腹が立つ: to be angry at X (a person, behaviour, or oneself). Mostly the speaker's own anger; for someone else's, 腹を立てる is usual.

near.diff: 頭に来る is casual and sudden, anger flaring up; 腹が立つ is the plain, all-purpose way to say something makes you angry.

cue: In calm, polite speech, tell a colleague how you felt when a friend cancelled by text an hour late without apologising.

ctx.s: 約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]られて、本当[ほんとう]に{腹[はら]が立[た]った}。
ctx.en: He broke his promise and I was really angry.

ctx.s: 「このような対応[たいおう]をされて、正直[しょうじき]{腹[はら]が立[た]ちました}。」
ctx.en: "To be honest, being treated like this made me angry."

ctx.s: 「ねえ、何[なに]がそんなに{腹[はら]が立[た]つ}の？」
ctx.en: "Hey, what is it that's making you so angry?"

ctx.s: 今[いま]でも、あの時[とき]のことを思[おも]い出[だ]すと{腹[はら]が立[た]って}くる。
ctx.en: Even now, when I remember that time I start to get angry.

ctx.s: 同[おな]じミスを繰[く]り返[かえ]す自分[じぶん]に{腹[はら]が立[た]って}、しばらく黙[だま]っていた。
ctx.en: I was angry with myself for making the same mistake again, and stayed silent for a while.

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]の言[い]い方[かた]には{腹[はら]が立[た]った}が、言[い]っていることは正[ただ]しかった。
ctx.en: His way of putting it made me angry, but what he said was right.

bad.s: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べなかったので、{腹[はら]が立[た]った}。
bad.en: (meant: I skipped breakfast, so I got hungry)
bad.why: Hara ga tatsu is anger, not the stomach. Getting hungry is onaka ga suku.

bad.s: 遅[おく]れて来[き]た彼[かれ]を{腹[はら]が立[た]った}。
bad.en: (meant: I got angry at him for being late)
bad.why: The target of the anger takes ni, not o: okurete kita kare ni hara ga tatta.

mean: to have a feeling that something is so
lit: a feeling does (it): the mind senses something without proof

use.how: A clause goes before it: 雨が降る気がする, 会ったような気がする. A soft, unsure way to state a hunch or impression.

near.diff: 気がする puts forward a hunch; 気のせい dismisses a feeling as having no basis.

cue: You're not sure, but that stranger's face seems familiar. Say so without claiming you know them.

ctx.s: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るような{気[き]がする}。
ctx.en: I have a feeling it's going to rain tomorrow.

ctx.s: この人[ひと]、どこかで会[あ]った{気[き]がする}。
ctx.en: I feel like I've met this person somewhere.

ctx.s: 「なんだか今日[きょう]はいいことがありそうな{気[き]がする}ね。」
ctx.en: "Somehow I feel like something good is going to happen today."

ctx.s: 鍵[かぎ]をかけ忘[わす]れた{気[き]がして}、家[いえ]に戻[もど]った。
ctx.en: I had a feeling I'd forgotten to lock up, so I went back home.

ctx.s: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]してから、時間[じかん]が経[た]つのが早[はや]くなった{気[き]がする}。
ctx.en: Since I moved, it feels like time passes faster.

ctx.s: 彼女[かのじょ]の話[はなし]を聞[き]いて、少[すこ]し救[すく]われたような{気[き]がした}。
ctx.en: Hearing her story, I felt a little as if I'd been rescued.

bad.s: 私[わたし]は{気[き]がする}、彼[かれ]は来[こ]ない。
bad.en: (meant: I have a feeling he won't come)
bad.why: The content of the feeling must come before ki ga suru: kare wa konai ki ga suru.

bad.s: あの人[ひと]は先生[せんせい]の{気[き]がする}。
bad.en: (meant: I have a feeling that person is a teacher)
bad.why: A noun cannot join with no here. Say sensei no you na ki ga suru, or sensei da to iu ki ga suru.

mean: to take a liking to, to be pleased with
lit: to enter the mind: something fits your taste and is let in

use.how: Xが/を気に入る: to come to like a particular thing you have met or chosen. A lasting liking is 気に入っている; a long-held general taste is 好き.

cue: You gave your niece a scarf, and she has worn it every day since. Tell her parents you're glad.

ctx.s: このかばん、とても{気[き]に入[い]って}いる。
ctx.en: I really love this bag.

ctx.s: 新[あたら]しい部屋[へや]が{気[き]に入[い]った}ので、すぐに契約[けいやく]した。
ctx.en: I liked the new flat, so I signed the contract straight away.

ctx.s: 「プレゼント、{気[き]に入[い]って}もらえてよかった。」
ctx.en: "I'm so glad you liked the present."

ctx.s: 「どれでも{気[き]に入[い]った}ものを選[えら]んでください。」
ctx.en: "Please choose whichever one you like."

ctx.s: 何度[なんど]描[か]き直[なお]しても、自分[じぶん]の絵[え]が{気[き]に入[い]らない}。
ctx.en: No matter how many times I redraw it, I'm not happy with my picture.

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]は社長[しゃちょう]に{気[き]に入[い]られて}、すぐに昇進[しょうしん]した。
ctx.en: The company president took a liking to him, and he was soon promoted.

bad.s: 私[わたし]は子[こ]どもの時[とき]から寿司[すし]が{気[き]に入[い]る}。
bad.en: (meant: I've liked sushi since I was a child)
bad.why: The plain form ki ni iru is not a lasting state, and a lifelong taste is suki: sushi ga suki da.

bad.s: 先生[せんせい]の説明[せつめい]に{気[き]に入[い]った}。
bad.en: (meant: I liked the teacher's explanation)
bad.why: The thing liked takes ga or o, not ni: sensei no setsumei ga ki ni itta.

mean: to worry about something, to take it to heart
lit: to make (something) into the mind: put your thoughts on it on purpose

use.how: Xを気にする: to mind or fret about X (looks, others' opinions, a mistake). 気にしないで is the everyday 'don't worry about it'.

near.diff: 気になる is something catching your attention by itself (が); 気にする is you dwelling on it (を), often more than you should.

cue: A friend apologises again and again for spilling a drop of tea on your table. Tell them it's nothing.

ctx.s: 「大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]、{気[き]にしないで}。」
ctx.en: "It's fine, don't worry about it."

ctx.s: 彼女[かのじょ]は人[ひと]の目[め]をとても{気[き]にする}。
ctx.en: She worries a lot about what other people think.

ctx.s: 年齢[ねんれい]なんて{気[き]にする}必要[ひつよう]はないよ。
ctx.en: There's no need to worry about your age.

ctx.s: 「体重[たいじゅう]、{気[き]にしてる}の？全然[ぜんぜん]太[ふと]ってないよ。」
ctx.en: "Are you worried about your weight? You haven't put on any at all."

ctx.s: 小[ちい]さなミスをいつまでも{気[き]にして}いたら、前[まえ]に進[すす]めない。
ctx.en: If you keep dwelling on small mistakes forever, you can't move forward.

ctx.s: 父[ちち]は値段[ねだん]を{気[き]にせず}、一番[いちばん]いいワインを注文[ちゅうもん]した。
ctx.en: Without caring about the price, my father ordered the best wine.

bad.s: 明日[あした]の天気[てんき]が{気[き]にする}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm wondering about tomorrow's weather)
bad.why: Ki ni suru takes o, with a person as subject. With ga, use ki ni naru: ashita no tenki ga ki ni naru.

bad.s: 雪[ゆき]だから、運転[うんてん]は{気[き]にして}ね。
bad.en: (meant: it's snowing, so drive carefully)
bad.why: Ki ni suru is worrying, not taking care. Being careful is ki o tsukeru: unten ni ki o tsukete ne.

lit: the mind gets attached: your attention suddenly lands on something

use.how: Xに気がつく: to notice or realise X; same as 気づく. 気がつくと／気がついたら also means 'before I knew it' or 'when I came to'.

near.diff: 気が利く praises someone for thoughtfully doing what others need; 気がつく is simply noticing.

cue: Halfway to the station you realise your wallet is still on the kitchen table. Say when it struck you.

ctx.s: 財布[さいふ]を忘[わす]れたことに、駅[えき]で{気[き]がついた}。
ctx.en: I realised at the station that I'd forgotten my wallet.

ctx.s: 髪[かみ]を切[き]ったのに、誰[だれ]も{気[き]がつかなかった}。
ctx.en: I'd had my hair cut, but nobody noticed.

ctx.s: 「間違[まちが]いに{気[き]がついたら}、教[おし]えてください。」
ctx.en: "If you notice any mistakes, please let me know."

ctx.s: ゲームをしていて、{気[き]がついたら}もう夜中[よなか]の二時[にじ]だった。
ctx.en: I was playing a game, and before I knew it, it was two in the morning.

ctx.s: 事故[じこ]のあと、{気[き]がつくと}病院[びょういん]のベッドの上[うえ]だった。
ctx.en: After the accident, when I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed.

ctx.s: 失[うしな]って初[はじ]めて、家族[かぞく]の大切[たいせつ]さに{気[き]がついた}。
ctx.en: Only after losing them did I realise how precious my family was.

bad.s: 授業[じゅぎょう]では先生[せんせい]の話[はなし]をよく{気[き]がついて}ください。
bad.en: (meant: in class, please listen carefully to the teacher)
bad.why: Ki ga tsuku is noticing that happens to you; it cannot take o or be a deliberate effort. Say sensei no hanashi o yoku kiite kudasai.

bad.s: 私[わたし]は毎朝[まいあさ]七時[しちじ]に{気[き]がつく}。
bad.en: (meant: I wake up at seven every morning)
bad.why: Coming to is only after fainting or the like. Waking up normally is me ga sameru or okiru.

lit: the fault of the mind: blame the feeling, not the facts

use.how: A noun phrase: 気のせいだ, 気のせいじゃない？. 気のせいか、～ opens a remark the speaker is not sure of.

near.diff: 気がする states a hunch; 気のせい says a feeling is groundless.

cue: Your friend jumps at a creak in the dark flat and asks if someone's there. Reassure them it's nothing.

ctx.s: 「今[いま]、誰[だれ]かいなかった？」「{気[き]のせい}だよ。」
ctx.en: "Wasn't someone there just now?" "You're imagining things."

ctx.s: 「ちょっと痩[や]せた？」「{気[き]のせい}じゃない？変[か]わってないよ。」
ctx.en: "Have you lost weight?" "Isn't that just your imagination? I haven't changed."

ctx.s: {気[き]のせい}か、今日[きょう]は駅[えき]がいつもより静[しず]かだ。
ctx.en: Maybe it's just me, but the station seems quieter than usual today.

ctx.s: 物音[ものおと]が聞[き]こえたと思[おも]ったが、{気[き]のせい}だったようだ。
ctx.en: I thought I heard a noise, but it seems it was just my imagination.

ctx.s: 「{気[き]のせい}かもしれないけど、最近[さいきん]元気[げんき]ないね。」
ctx.en: "Maybe I'm imagining it, but you've seemed down lately."

ctx.s: 熱[ねつ]っぽいのは{気[き]のせい}ではなかった。体温計[たいおんけい]は三十八度[さんじゅうはちど]だった。
ctx.en: Feeling feverish wasn't just my imagination: the thermometer read thirty-eight degrees.

bad.s: 試験[しけん]に落[お]ちたのは私[わたし]の{気[き]のせい}だ。
bad.en: (meant: failing the exam is my own fault)
bad.why: Ki no sei means a feeling is imagined, not blame. 'My fault' is watashi no sei.

bad.s: この部屋[へや]は{気[き]のせい}が悪[わる]い。
bad.en: (meant: this room has a bad atmosphere)
bad.why: Ki no sei is a fixed phrase for imagination, not atmosphere. Say fun'iki ga warui.

mean: to lend a hand, to help someone with a task
lit: to lend one's hand: give someone the use of your hands for a while

use.how: Xに手を貸す: help X with a task, often physical. 手を貸してくれない？ asks for help; Xに手を貸す can also mean being complicit in something bad.

near.diff: 手を出す is getting involved in something, meddling, or hitting someone; 手を貸す is helping.

cue: You're struggling to carry a heavy box up the stairs and your flatmate walks past. Ask them for help.

ctx.s: 「ちょっと{手[て]を貸[か]して}くれない？この箱[はこ]、重[おも]くて。」
ctx.en: "Could you give me a hand? This box is heavy."

ctx.s: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しの時[とき]、友達[ともだち]が{手[て]を貸[か]して}くれた。
ctx.en: When I moved, my friends lent a hand.

ctx.s: 階段[かいだん]の前[まえ]でお年寄[としよ]りが困[こま]っていたので、{手[て]を貸[か]した}。
ctx.en: An elderly person was having trouble at the stairs, so I helped them.

ctx.s: 「一人[ひとり]で大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]？」「うん、でも後[あと]で{手[て]を貸[か]して}もらうかも。」
ctx.en: "Can you manage on your own?" "Yes, but I might need your help later."

ctx.s: 困[こま]っている人[ひと]がいたら、{手[て]を貸[か]す}のは当然[とうぜん]だ。
ctx.en: If someone is in trouble, helping them is only natural.

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]は知[し]らないうちに詐欺[さぎ]に{手[て]を貸[か]して}いた。
ctx.en: Without realising it, he had been helping with a fraud.

bad.s: 宿題[しゅくだい]は兄[あに]に{手[て]を貸[か]した}。
bad.en: (meant: my older brother helped me with my homework)
bad.why: This says I helped my brother. Being helped is ani ni te o kashite moratta, or simply tetsudatte moratta.

bad.s: 財布[さいふ]を忘[わす]れたので、友達[ともだち]が千円[せんえん]{手[て]を貸[か]して}くれた。
bad.en: (meant: I forgot my wallet, so a friend lent me a thousand yen)
bad.why: Te o kasu is help with a task, never money. Lending money is okane o kasu: sen'en kashite kureta.

mean: to show up, to put in an appearance
lit: to put out one's face: let people see you there, if only for a moment

use.how: Xに顔を出す: to drop in at a gathering or place, often briefly or out of goodwill. Not for formal attendance where you play the main part.

near.diff: 足を運ぶ stresses making the trip to a place on purpose; 顔を出す is showing up at a gathering, often just briefly.

cue: You're busy on the night of your old school reunion, but you plan to drop in for half an hour to say hello.

ctx.s: 「時間[じかん]があったら、パーティーに{顔[かお]を出[だ]して}ね。」
ctx.en: "If you have time, do drop by the party."

ctx.s: 忙[いそが]しいけど、同窓会[どうそうかい]には少[すこ]しだけ{顔[かお]を出[だ]す}つもりだ。
ctx.en: I'm busy, but I plan to show up at the reunion for a little while.

ctx.s: 最近[さいきん]、全然[ぜんぜん]実家[じっか]に{顔[かお]を出[だ]して}いない。
ctx.en: Lately I haven't been home to see my parents at all.

ctx.s: 「たまには部活[ぶかつ]に{顔[かお]を出[だ]せ}よ。みんな待[ま]ってるぞ。」
ctx.en: "Show up at club practice once in a while. Everyone's waiting for you."

ctx.s: 彼[かれ]は仕事[しごと]帰[がえ]りに、よくこの居酒屋[いざかや]に{顔[かお]を出[だ]す}。
ctx.en: He often drops in at this pub on his way home from work.

ctx.s: 新[あたら]しい店長[てんちょう]は、近[ちか]くに来[き]たついでに取引先[とりひきさき]へ{顔[かお]を出[だ]した}。
ctx.en: Since he was in the area anyway, the new manager dropped in on a supplier.

bad.s: 昨日[きのう]、会社[かいしゃ]の飲[の]み会[かい]を{顔[かお]を出[だ]した}。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday I showed up at the office drinks)
bad.why: Kao o dasu already has its o; the place you show up at takes ni: nomikai ni kao o dashita.

bad.s: 明日[あした]は大事[だいじ]な面接[めんせつ]なので、必[かなら]ず{顔[かお]を出[だ]します}。
bad.en: (meant: tomorrow is an important interview, so I'll definitely attend)
bad.why: Kao o dasu suggests a casual, brief appearance, wrong for your own job interview. Say mensetsu o ukemasu, or kanarazu ikimasu.
